nagabe.reason: Designed colour taken to its most economical: red, black and jade, hard graphic shadow, almost screen-print. Shares the graphic-invention pole (Mika Pikazo, redjuice) but with none of the luminous-girl idiom — a deliberate stretch in subject and palette.

Anders Zorn.reason: The bravura-line ancestor of Fechin and Nick Alm, and bathers in moving water — the Monks/Mieno interest in figures seen through water, drawn with a needle instead of a brush.

James McNeill Whistler.reason: Haze and night as the whole subject — the atmosphere side of the collection (Baugh, Mieno) a century earlier, with almost nothing described.

Winslow Homer.reason: Water and weather handled in transparent washes — light on the sea as the subject; also a painter who began as a magazine illustrator.

John Singer Sargent.reason: The source Lipking and Schmid both point back to: alla prima confidence and light on white fabric.

Hiroshi Yoshida.reason: Printmaking wildcard: lamplit canals and night streets built from flat, graded woodblock colour — atmosphere and light without a figure, from the same country as the hush cluster.

Vilhelm Hammershøi.reason: Sprick's 'air doing something' in a room, pushed to silence — the Morimoto hush without the figure.

Mary Cassatt.reason: Quiet domestic figures in printmaking — the hush cluster's subject in line and flat colour.

toi8.reason: The Kantoku/深崎暮人 idiom with more air and less rendering — pale line, pale light, figures that sit quietly in the white of the page.

Loish.reason: Luminous illustration from outside the Japanese idiom: backlit figures, water and starlight done as designed colour and flowing shape rather than rendered detail.

Yuko Shimizu.reason: Graphic invention in ink: the energy and designed colour of the Yoneyama/Mika Pikazo pole, but carried by a brush line with ukiyo-e ancestry.

James Jean.reason: Sits on the line between the two tabs: painted on canvas, but with an illustrator's invented colour and ornament — luminous without being photographic.

Kilian Eng.reason: Wildcard: no figures to speak of, but atmosphere and designed colour at full strength — haze, scale and a strictly limited print palette.

Sachin Teng.reason: Graphic invention and pattern — cover work with the same designed-colour logic as redjuice and Mika Pikazo, drawn from a different tradition.

MANOdeMARINA.reason: Designed colour reduced to two or three flat inks and a lot of white — the graphic-invention pole (Mika Pikazo, redjuice) crossed with poster design.

Canis Albus.reason: Wildcard: staged, theatrical solemnity (the Kamoi/Ferri appetite for performed feeling) transposed onto dogs in the format of religious icons — deadpan, tender and odd.

Mengxuan Li.reason: Light and colour carrying the whole picture with the figure small or absent — the loundraw instinct applied to plants and water.

Henrik Aa. Uldalen.reason: Staged, lit figures against darkness — the Currie/Lorca line — but with the figure literally breaking up into brushwork.

Șerban Savu.reason: Atmosphere and quiet at landscape scale: haze, muted light, small figures — the hush without a close-up face, in a subject the collection had never touched.

Harding Meyer.reason: The face seen through something again — here the interference is the brushwork itself, like Mieno's water rebuilt as paint marks.

Michael Carson.reason: Nick Alm's social scenes and Assael's caught-not-posed figures, with more graphic, flattened grounds and fashion-plate poise.

Chie Yoshii.reason: Theatrical, staged figuration (Lorca, Ferri) crossed with Japanese folk tales — ornament and invented colour in oil.

Joseph Lorusso.reason: Lamplight and interior warmth — the quiet-figure line with amber light instead of Morimoto's grey.

Kamome Shirahama.reason: Luminous illustration by way of pen-and-ink: ornamental line and printed-looking colour, closer to golden-age book illustration than to anime rendering.

mocha.reason: loundraw's atmosphere with the figure almost gone: skies, reflections and station platforms at dusk — light and air as the whole subject.

コーラ.reason: Night reflections and low sun painted by someone whose job is atmosphere — the background-art craft behind the luminous-illustration idiom.

Annie Stegg Gerard.reason: Staged, lit figures in the Lorca/Ferri line, but pastoral rather than dark: folklore theatre in a Rococo palette.

Arthur Gain.reason: Alla prima portraits with visible, confident brushwork — the Schmid/Blokhin handling in the present tense, and a working teacher.

Michael C Hayes.reason: Theatrical figures lit against darkness, painted for fantasy illustration — illustration that is traditional oil and charcoal.

Wayne Haag.reason: Wildcard: vast hazy landscapes and tiny figures — atmosphere and scale over portraiture, painted in oil by a film concept artist.

Daniel Danger.reason: Printmaking wildcard: night atmosphere from a few flat inks — Whistler's nocturnes as a screen print.

ゆずききの.reason: The weightless, high-key light of loundraw and 白身魚 at its most distilled — cloud, moon and water in pale blues.

すり餌.reason: Line-led, near-monochrome figures with a few spot colours — graphic restraint (redjuice) crossed with the delicacy of the hush cluster.

わいっしゅ.reason: Dense, lamplit cityscapes and towers in haze — atmosphere and light built as architecture, the background craft behind luminous illustration.

こまちみゆた.reason: Traditional illustration with a light, patient brush — quiet like the hush cluster, but botanical, humorous and hand-painted rather than rendered.

はねこと.reason: The backlit after-school idiom of カントク and 深崎暮人 — soft rim light, reflections, sunflowers — but with more sky and water around the figure.

ときわた.reason: Designed colour held to one palette — the LAM/redjuice discipline of a limited, artificial colour scheme.

ぶくろて.reason: Graphic invention in character design: flat colour, sharp silhouettes and a lot of white — closer to fashion plates than to rendered anime.

Quang Ho.reason: The Schmid/Lipking handling at full strength — shapes, edges and colour doing the work, with the same painterly ease across figures, snow and flowers.

Casey Childs.reason: The hush in an American key — a figure alone in a room with one source of light, soft edges and a still, withheld mood.
